newsitem.title: USA: MCI offers local phone service in NYC area.
newsitem.headline: MCI offers local phone service in NYC area.

text.p: Long distance phone operator MCI Communications Corp on Friday launched local residential telephone service in the New York City area.

In a news release, MCI said customers choosing it over NYNEX Corp will pay 30 cents less per month in line fees than they currently pay the local Baby Bell operator. MCI said it will charge $6.30 per month while the NYNEX line rate is $6.60.

MCI also said its plans to offer local service beyond the New York metropolitan area have been hampered by NYNEX. The complaint is virtually identical to objections it has raised about other Baby Bell operators around the country as MCI struggles to enter the $90-100 billion local phone service market.

The substance of MCI's complaint is that NYNEX is not providing an adequate electronic interface to facilitate the switch of customers to MCI from NYNEX. It claims that as a result it takes three times as long for a customer to order local service from MCI than it does from NYNEX.
"NYNEX isn't playing fair," MCI's executive director of brand marketing Judy Levine said.
NYNEX's Varettoni called the MCI assertion "absolutely false," noting that there are 25 other local companies in New York doing just what MCI says they'll have difficulty doing.
